title: Option-wrapping of fields documented as null-equiv-empty forces every caller to write the same null-check
description:
crate-jmap-types/src/methods.rs documents several fields as having
\"null on the wire is equivalent to empty\" semantics yet exposes them
as `Option<...>`, forcing every caller to write the same null check:

- `GetResponse.not_found: Option<Vec<Id>>` (methods.rs:55):
  doc-comment says \"`null` on the wire is treated as an empty list per
  RFC 8620 §5.1\". But the typed shape forces:
      if let Some(nf) = &resp.not_found { for id in nf { ... } }
  rather than the simpler:
      for id in &resp.not_found { ... }

- `SetResponse.created: Option<HashMap<String, T>>` (methods.rs:274),
  `SetResponse.updated: Option<HashMap<Id, Option<T>>>` (methods.rs:278),
  `SetResponse.destroyed: Option<Vec<Id>>` (methods.rs:280),
  `SetResponse.not_created/not_updated/not_destroyed: Option<HashMap<_, SetError>>`
  (methods.rs:282-286): every one of these is documented as describing
  \"successful X / failed X\" — `None` and `Some(empty_map)` are
  semantically identical (no successes / no failures). The doc-comments
  don't say it explicitly, but RFC 8620 §5.3 mandates the equivalence.

What a caller depending on this API in production accepts:

1. Six fields require the same `Option`-flattening idiom. A typical
   `/set` handler that wants to enumerate every result for logging
   writes the same 4 `if let Some` blocks every time.
2. Test code that builds a `SetResponse` for assertions writes
   `Some(HashMap::new())` or `Some(vec![])` constantly. Default
   constructors of the type would emit `None`; tests then have to
   wrap or unwrap.
3. The `null` wire-form contract is documented in prose; the type
   shape doesn't enforce that the caller treats `None` and `Some(empty)`
   as identical. A caller distinguishing them in a `match` produces a
   bug invisible to the type system.

Fix candidates:
- Change to `#[serde(default)] pub not_found: Vec<Id>` (and same for
  the SetResponse maps). Deserialize from `null` and from missing both
  yield empty. Serializing `Vec::new()` emits `[]` on the wire (or
  with `skip_serializing_if = \"Vec::is_empty\"`, omits the field). The
  wire shape changes (`[]` instead of `null`) but downstream
  servers/clients that follow RFC 8620 \"treat null as empty\" don't
  care.
- Or: keep `Option<Vec>` and provide accessor helpers like
  `pub fn not_found(&self) -> &[Id]` that auto-flatten. Cheaper to add,
  but still leaves the `pub` field as the trapdoor for callers who
  ignore the helper.

This applies to *every* `Option<Vec<T>>` / `Option<HashMap<...>>`
field in the methods.rs response types where RFC 8620 documents the
null-equiv-empty equivalence.
